Acrylic paint-along · beginner

A red sailboat on teal water at sunset

Start on a plain white canvas. Paint the sky first, then each part of the scene from farthest to nearest, each straight over the one behind it. Then the main subject, texture with simple brush moves, shadows, and highlights last.

3 stepsCanvas: 14 x 11 inFocal point: the sailboat Light: the setting sun, centerHow this lesson was made

What you need

Tubes

  • Titanium white
  • Cadmium yellow medium (hue)
  • Cadmium red medium (hue)
  • Ultramarine blue
  • Burnt sienna

Brushes

  • 1 inch flat: the skyFlat: square end, for big areas and straight edges
  • #6 round: the boatRound: pointed tip, thin or thick depending on how hard you press

Also

  • A 14 x 11 in canvas, landscape (hang it that way). Positions in the steps are percentages across and down: each 10% is 1.4 in across and 1.1 in down.
  • Water jar and paper towel
  • Palette or paper plate for mixing

Your paints

Every paint in the lesson. You don't have to mix them all at the start: each step lists the paints it uses with their recipes, so you can mix a little as you go before it dries. Parts are by volume.

Sunset orange3 parts red, 2 parts yellow, 2 parts white

Dusk violet3 parts ultramarine, 3 parts white, 1 part red
the top of the sky · First needed in step 1
Deep teal3 parts ultramarine, 1 part yellow, 1 part white
the water · First needed in step 2
Boat red1 part red, a touch of ultramarine
the hull · First needed in step 3
Sail white6 parts white, 1 part burnt sienna, a touch of yellow
the sail · First needed in step 3

How the paint recipes were worked out5 paints, free

Paint doesn't mix like light on a screen: blue and yellow make green, not gray. So the recipes come from a pigment mixing model (Mixbox), not a guess. For each paint it tried every simple recipe from your tubes, up to three colors plus white, and kept the one that lands closest to the color in the painting. Delta E is how far off it lands: under 2 is hard to see, under 5 is close, and over 8 means these tubes can't quite make it.

  • Sunset orange Delta E 1.5
    in the paintingthe recipe mixed

    Mixer: 3 parts red, 2 parts yellow, 2 parts white

    Written by eye first: yellow, a touch of red, white

  • Dusk violet Delta E 2.0
    in the paintingthe recipe mixed

    Mixer: 3 parts ultramarine, 3 parts white, 1 part red

    Written by eye first: blue, red, white

  • Deep teal Delta E 6.2
    in the paintingthe recipe mixed

    Mixer: 3 parts ultramarine, 1 part yellow, 1 part white

    Written by eye first: blue, yellow, a touch of black

  • Boat red Delta E 5.7
    in the paintingthe recipe mixed

    Mixer: 1 part red, a touch of ultramarine

    Written by eye first: red, a touch of black

  • Sail white Delta E 2.2
    in the paintingthe recipe mixed

    Mixer: 6 parts white, 1 part burnt sienna, a touch of yellow

    Written by eye first: white, a touch of yellow

Furthest off: Delta E 6.2. Real tubes vary by brand, so mix, compare with the step picture, and nudge.

What the reviewer caught3 notes

A second Claude, with fresh eyes and none of this reasoning, compared each picture with its neighbors and the finish. It gets two rounds of fixes, then stops; anything still off is flagged on its step. A third checked each step's words against a measured map of what the picture changed, asking whether a beginner following them would get there.

  • Finish check The sun is a touch smaller than in the photo.
  • Round 1 Step 2: The horizon tilts a little. (left)
  • Text check: flat Step 1: No glow named (fixed)
